1.why: Verify-token compares the supplied code only to the recovery token stored on the caller’s own session and requires recovery.real for that session.

2.why: Tokens live only on the initiating session; another user/session has a different recovery object, so the same code does not authenticate for them.

3.why: password-update only flips recovery.passwordUpdated and rehashes the password; no other sessions are deleted or de-authenticated.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set; the exact TLS version is not pinned in code but HTTPS is required.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and session recovery fields are stored in plaintext in memory, not encrypted.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API returns testDeliveryToken in JSON and the client logs it, so the reset secret is not guarded in the delivery path.

7.why: Email/token/password inputs are format-validated server-side and all dynamic DOM updates use textContent, preventing script injection.

8.why: There are no user-controlled redirect parameters or open-redirect responses anywhere in the server or client.

9.why: There are no server email templates that interpolate user input; delivery is only a client-side simulation.

10.why: Recovery tokens and MFA codes are returned as testDeliveryToken/testMfaCode and appended to the on-page Logs list.

11.why: Updated passwords use bcrypt, but the initial password hash and the fixed mfaCode "481516" are embedded in source.

12.why: A fixed initial bcrypt hash is shipped in code with no separate ban on well-known/default passwords beyond normal login checks.

13.why: allowed() rate-limits each action to 5 attempts per 15-minute window then blocks for 15 minutes.

14.why: initiate always returns the same generic "If an account can use that address..." message whether or not the email matches EMAIL.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte values from randomBytes (64 hex chars), single-session, and checked with timingSafeEqual.
